subject.title: fix(infra): fix exec-approvals async lock, not just the sync path (#106777, extends #108971)

question: Should exec approvals own this local asynchronous nonce-lock implementation, or should the shared `@openclaw/fs-safe` lock be corrected and consumed with its established authorization guarantees?
rationale: The change moves policy-store locking out of the shared implementation and asserts equivalence for a fail-closed authorization boundary; source tests alone cannot choose the intended long-term owner or contract.

options.title: Validate and retain a local lock
options.body: Approve local ownership only after an owner verifies parity for stale recovery, symlink/path safety, and re-entrancy, with real Docker/VirtioFS proof attached.

options.title: Fix the shared lock instead
options.body: Keep exec approvals on the shared helper and pursue a dependency-level nonce ownership repair if the shared contract is intended to apply uniformly.

recommendation.title: Validate and retain a local lock
recommendation.body: Approve local ownership only after an owner verifies parity for stale recovery, symlink/path safety, and re-entrancy, with real Docker/VirtioFS proof attached.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the identified contributor for the related nonce-lock design and are the closest available routing candidate for the intended lock contract.
